sharedProofs.proof: Configuration adds PRE beforeP1 and POST afterP5 only for effective LEFT/DOWN/UP. retrieveProcessors sorts enum ordinals; PRE0 precedes all applicable beforeP1 processors and POST58 follows all afterP5 processors. Actual factory creates PRE with TO_INPUT_DIRECTION and POST with TO_INTERNAL_LTR: do not infer mode from names. With default READING_DIRECTION, process_12 uses LEFT mirrorX, DOWN transpose, and UP Y->T in pre versus T->Y in post. ROTATION else branch is explicitly not admitted. prepare resolves UNDEFINED once with getDirection_1/default aspect literal>=1, keeping explicit original direction thereafter. createPort/fromDirection produces original output sides E/W/S/N, and transforms, not import shortcuts, map them to the LTR core frame. One global PROCESSORS/flags/RNG context is inherited by components, including components without local loops. layout_1 cleanup occurs only after POST; component combine/resize are distinct later components.

sharedProofs.proof: MapPropertyHolder.getProperty returns a nonnull current value; otherwise Property.getDefault clones only values implementing actual GWT type4, via the exact registered concrete runtime class. KVector(type8/type4) registry lambda1->$clone_1->new KVector_1 and ElkPadding(class105 inheritsSpacing215/type4) registry lambda7->new ElkPadding_1->Spacing_0 are nonnull fresh independent copies; getProperty stores these cloned objects. Therefore A get_node_size_minimum(node) materializes a per-node Vec2(0,0), and get_node_labels_padding(element) materializes per-holder Insets(5 each). Subsequent getter returns same stored object. Graph mirror/transpose mutates NLPadding in place; transposeProperties reads minimum and ALWAYS replaces it with a NEW swapped vector, even zero or same-valued. Never alias a module-level default. Scalar enums do not type4-clone/store; absent ALIGNMENT(defaultUNDEFINED)/PORT_INDEX(defaultnull) stays absent unless a literal branch writes it. EnumSet defaults are not assumed clone/store merely because mutable; label-placement branch is guarded by actual hasProperty first.

sharedProofs.proof: Fresh implicit endpoint ports have zero size/anchor and explicitlySuppliedPortAnchor=false. setSide always assigns side, then assigns anchor using the NEW port size: NORTH=(w/2,0), EAST=(w,h/2), SOUTH=(w/2,h), WEST=(0,h/2). Source transforms first mutate port pos/anchor and (transpose) size, then call this setter, so the anchor reset must not be omitted or moved. This extends to temporarily hidden/restored loop ports: direction PRE precedes hide and POST follows final restore, and their current geometry is transformed in the same outgoing-edge iteration. Do not change owner/endpoint pointers or rebuild adjacency. Default ports remain implicit; public nonzero/explicit anchors remain outside scope.

sharedProofs.proof: Public labels/ports/nesting and external-port dummies are excluded. Retained LongEdge dummies are LONG_EDGE, not EXTERNAL_PORT, and are removed before POST. Node/port/edge label arrays are empty; no label loop creates geometry. Input basic-nine keys do not include NODE_LABELS_PLACEMENT, ALIGNMENT, POSITION or PORT_INDEX. Node label-placement helpers check hasProperty before any read; default empty placement does not manufacture a property merely by Java mutable intuition. Retained processors do not install a nonempty node placement property. A host phase guard rejects unsupported nonempty placement, explicit position/index/alignment or external type rather than inventing those omitted branches. NODE_SIZE_MINIMUM and NLPadding are separately supported real writes, not rejected because they were absent before direction PRE.

guards: E07 common raw and per-phase domain; default READING_DIRECTION with original graph.DIRECTION preserved.
PRE only original NORMAL nodes (loops still attached), POST only restored original NORMAL nodes/edges after LongJoin/LoopPost/ReversedRestorer; layerless+layers gathered in source order.
All source-used coordinates finite. Zero dimensions, negative temporary pre coordinates, tiny values and asymmetric padding retained; no nonnegative temporary-position assumption.
No public labels/ports/nesting, external port dummies or nondefault alignment/position/index/placement overrides.

guardProofs.proof: Build nodes from source layerless+layers. If graph.size.x==0, offset=max(0, successive ((node.pos.x+node.size.x)+node.margin.right)) then subtract graph.offset.x; otherwise offset=graph.size.x-graph.offset.x then subtract graph.offset.x AGAIN. Mutate node.pos.x=(offset-node.width)-oldX, swap node.padding.left/right; source optional alignment/position/placement branches are guarded. For each current port mutate pos.x=(node.width-port.width)-oldX then anchor.x=port.width-oldAnchorX then setSide(E<->W, N/S unchanged), with actual implicit-anchor reset. For each outgoing edge mutate every bend.x=offset-oldX in place, then call the real JP getter even if absent and iterate its truthy (possibly empty) chain. Original edge list/bend order/endpoints/JP identity remain. Last swap graph.padding.left/right and get/mutate per-holder NLPadding.left/right. Do not change graph.size/offset, node.margin, layer.size/order, or reverse any chain. PRELEFT and POSTLEFT execute this identical literal helper on different actual states; no proof of floating identity from double reflection is used.

reads: Per-holder padding and optional scalar properties
writes: Outgoing bend/JP x in place; absent JP/default NLPadding materialize

guardedOutHelpers.guard: Only EXTERNAL_PORT branch; no external dummies/public ports/nesting.

numericSemantics.floating: Python binary64 operations preserve each source subtraction/addition/max/swap order. Mirror graph-size==0 branch and (size-offset)-offset order retained, without algebraic normalization, tolerance changes or rounding. Swaps use temporaries. Source setter reset occurs after geometry transform.

guardProofs.proof: Assign actual LNode.id in CURRENT layerless order globally once. DFS scans each current ordered port incoming-before-outgoing and marks visited; loops cannot duplicate a node. For each newly discovered component, prepend only when its size is STRICTLY larger than the current first component, otherwise append. This is not a full descending-size sort: order3,2,4,3 yields4,3,2,3; equal maximum components retain discovery order. Execute every resulting component independently: new NGraph/NNodes/each distinct parallel nonself NEdge, local private IDs and ordered incoming-then-outgoing incident caches, iterationLimit=28*round(sqrt(component.size)), then actual NS solver with balancingtrue. Do not flatten all components into one private tree and do not skip isolate solves. Write each private origin into the existing global LGraph.layers, appending to existing layer node lists in private NNode order, growing the list only as needed. After ALL components clear original layerlessNodes and per-call scratch state. Empty input returns early without constructing a private graph.

Topological FIFO gives feasible integer ranks for unit delta on a DAG. Tight DFS rooted at the FIRST private node grows only to non-tree nodes or traverses already marked tree edges. If its node count<n, weak connectivity supplies a crossing edge; minimal nonnegative slack with the source orientation sign shifts the current tree, preserves feasibility, and makes at least one new crossing edge tight. At most n-1 node additions produce a connected tight spanning tree. Every true tree edge has directed rank difference1. No assumption that the first node is a source is permitted. Parallel edges do not invalidate the tree argument: source tightTreeDFS may choose only an edge to a previously non-tree node (or traverse an already-selected treeEdge). A second same-endpoint edge to the now-tree node is not inserted as an extra tree edge. Each parallel constraint is still checked separately by slack/topological indegree loops.

Compute actual postorder intervals and leaf-propagated cutvalues in source list order. For a tree edge, endpoint subtree intervals are nested: isInHead returns the component containing the directed target after deleting that edge. Preserve its literal condition. leaveEdge picks first insertion-ordered tree edge cut<-1e-10; enterEdge picks first strict-min slack crossing head->outside. Removing leave and adding enter retains a tree; shifting the outside by -slack makes enter tight while other tree edges keep difference1 and all directed edge spans stay>=1. Recompute postorder/cutvalues exactly. Degenerate exchanges still stop at the source iteration limit; do not continue to a textbook optimum. All parallel NEdges contribute their own unit weight to unknownCutvalues and cut sums. enterEdge still chooses the FIRST strict-min crossing edge in actual private edge order; an equal-span duplicate must not replace it. The tree is an identity set of selected NEdges, so deleting one edge and appending another preserves exact identity/order even for equal endpoint pairs.

A connected n-node tight tree with unit directed gaps has rank range<=n-1; a path between minimum and maximum visits every intervening integer rank, so CURRENT filling before balancing is nonempty in that local interval. Source balance moves only equal-degree nodes and only to a strictly smaller COMBINED filling. Such nodes either have incoming/outgoing neighbors or are the isolated singleton. minimalSpan literal ternary yields the true min incoming span and an outgoing bound no larger than the true min outgoing span (a non-min incoming edge may also reduce that bound). Thus candidate ranks stay strictly between predecessors and successors and within the original local normalized interval. The singleton range is empty. With previousLayeringNodeCounts=NULL, counts are current-only: each moved-from count>=2 leaves a current node, so this first/private-alone component retains every local layer. With NONNULL previous counts, a moved-from combined count>=2 may contain only one current node and previous nodes: that move can empty this PRIVATE component local rank but cannot empty the COMBINED/GLOBAL layer, because strict-lower destination counts are initially at least1. Earlier component nodes never move. The existing global layer interval remains filled; no new rank outside the current component original interval is selected. Do not claim every later private component has nonempty final occupancy at every rank, and do not rewrite the minimalSpan ternary. Multiplicity changes degree equality and candidate order but not per-edge unit feasibility or the conservative rank interval. Cyclic original direction and REVERSED provenance are not read by the private solver. NS7-G2 binds the actual cumulative counts and literal update order.

This phase runs BEFORE dummy creation, so n<=8 and m<=28. The literal >=40 removeSubtrees condition is false. Initial ranks are integers0..7. During at most7 feasible-tree growth shifts a loose range recurrence Rnext<=2R+1 bounds transient ranges below1024. After the tight tree exists its range is<=7; at most84 exchanges shift one cut by a crossing slack whose magnitude is<=6, so all temporary ranks have magnitude well below4096. Cutvalue sums are bounded integral combinations of at most28 unit edges on an8-node tree (a conservative bound28*2^8=7168 suffices); filling/IDs/counters also stay far below2^31 and2^53. Host exact integer arithmetic equals JS binary64 integer results here. The only sqrt/round operates on integer n1..8, away from half-integer rounding boundaries. These are source-derived bounds, not observed-coordinate tolerances.

For each connected private component, n_i original vertices and a unit tight spanning tree imply max normalized rank-min rank<=n_i-1 before balance: any two ranks differ by a signed sum of at most n_i-1 unit tree deltas. Normalization subtracts local minimum; balance only selects a feasible integer rank inside that same existing normalized interval, and previous-component filling affects only preferences. Therefore each nonself edge gap d<=n_i-1<=7. Every original nonself edge creates d-1<=max(n_i-2,0)<=6 long dummies and d proper segments. Sum multiplicity across ALL components, with total n<=8,m<=28: D<=6m<=168, total original-plus-dummy nodes<=176, nonloop proper segments<=m+D<=196, original+dummy ports<=2m+2D<=392. Loops only hide/restore their original ports and do not split; including loop count in m is conservative. No C(n,3) simple-graph bound, per-component multiplication of the whole raw budget, or observed-maximum shortcut is used. Empty/isolate components have no edge/dummy allocation. Global layer count is max component layercount<=8 because ranks reuse common layer indices; it is not the sum of component layercounts.

previousLayeringNodeCounts starts null for the first component. If total connectedComponents.size>1, after writing that component into global layers allocate a NEW int array of the current global layer-list length and snapshot each ACTUAL layer.nodes.length, including all previously solved components. Pass exactly that array into the next fresh private solver. normalize computes current local min/max, allocates local filling length highest-lowest+1 and counts current nodes; then adds previousCounts from index0, stopping when the local filling length is reached, even if previousCounts is longer. No concatenate/pad/global-private-tree substitute. balance uses this combined filling with the existing strict less-than comparison and source private node order/minimalSpan interval. Increment/decrement combined counts on moves, but write only this component node.rank; previous graph nodes are never moved by a later solve. This branch executes for multiple isolates too, with snapshots[1],[2],... and singleton local filling. Integer count sums remain<=8; no float tolerance or stochastic choice is involved.

Reviewed NS algorithm/driver/helpers read current incidence, default shortness and thoroughness; no size, position, margin, padding, DIRECTION or JavaRandom is read. E07 directions preserve endpoint identity and only alter geometry/side before this phase; they do not change unit rank constraints. Thus allow actual original DIRECTION values without writingRIGHT. Global original node IDs and REVERSED/CYCLIC flags remain real state; private graph IDs are independent per solve.

Geometry use is conditional on ORIGINAL REQUEST topology, never inferred from coordinates. (1) If an original weak component is a DAG and the separately reviewed default E07 GREEDY source/sink proof preserves all its directions, every original directed reachable pair has at least one unit-span path. Private feasibility gives target.rank-source.rank>=pathlength>=1. Previous-count balancing preserves every edge unit constraint by its source minimalSpan feasible interval, so reachable ranks remain different even if zero dimensions/spacing make geometric coordinates equal. (2) If an original weak component is a strict simple directed ring n_i>=2, exactly n_i edges and indeg/outdeg1 with no selfloop/duplicate/chord, separately reviewed GREEDY produces one reversed edge and a Hamiltonian forward path plus shortcut, irrespective of fallback choice/start or unrelated component processing. Its unit path forces rankspan>=n_i-1 and the tight tree bound forces<=n_i-1, so all path gaps1 and all vertices distinct. Every internal vertex has immediate predecessor/successor ranks, leaving no alternative minimalSpan rank; endpoints do not qualify for nontrivial balancing (including n_i2 parallel forward edges). Combined previous filling cannot move a ring vertex. Other weak components can change solver order, previous filling and which ring start RNG chooses, but cannot change these feasibility implications. Valid for separatefalse or true. This does not assert every pair in arbitrary SCC/mixed cycle or incomparable DAG pair is distinct, and never skips overlap/root bounds/section/endpoints/route checks.
